state.old_main: iter_sync.main() takes no arguments, reads sys.argv; successful command branches use bare return (None); sys.exit(1/2/3) escapes to imported caller; OSError/ValueError/RuntimeError are handled only in script __main__ guard.
state.candidate: iter_sync.main() lazily returns iter_cli.main(), so success returns 0 and formerly escaping exceptions become integer codes.
state.contract: iter_cli.main(argv: list[str] | None=None)->int is new; iter_sync retains old main() facade and imported function/class signatures and behavior.
state.available_dispatch: iter_cli._dispatch(argv) contains exact old dispatch body except copying argv and expanded help.

facade.instructions: Which facade behavior meets both the new integer CLI API and old imported main contract?

criteria.preserve: Legacy main lazily invokes _dispatch(sys.argv[1:]), keeping None/SystemExit/errors; restore old __main__ error wrapper. New public iter_cli.main returns integer.
criteria.integer: Legacy main returns new integer API result, accepting success/error behavior change.
